Chapter 7: Confronting Racism in Modern Times.
You know, it’s easy to imagine racism as something that only happened “back then”—a problem for the history books, not something we face today. But for so many people, the reality is much closer to home.
Sure, the headlines might change, but the patterns? They feel all too familiar. Maybe it’s someone being treated unfairly because of their skin color. Or a community targeted by hateful words or actions. Sometimes it’s just that nagging feeling a system is rigged against certain groups.
Picture a group of friends, sitting together, scrolling through their phones. They’re reading about a recent incident in the news—frustration, confusion, and even a sense of helplessness fill the room. One friend says, “Why does this keep happening?” Another points out, “The details are new, but the issues? They’re old.”
That’s when the conversation gets real: How do we move from outrage to action?
Racism today can hide behind polite words or complicated rules. It shows up in things like hiring decisions, who gets stopped by the police, or whose voices get heard—and whose get ignored. Sometimes, it’s just a joke that no one calls out, or a policy that sounds neutral but ends up hurting certain groups more.
Most folks don’t set out to be unfair, but the systems they live in can make it all too easy to look the other way.
And now, social media has completely changed the way we talk about race. Stories that might’ve been buried in the past can go viral in minutes—sparking conversations, and sometimes even protests. But with everything moving so fast, it’s tough to know what’s really true, or what you’re supposed to do next. Feeling overwhelmed? Yeah, you’re not alone. Sometimes it feels like nothing ever changes.
But here’s the thing: change does happen. When people come together—whether online or in real life—they can push for new laws, demand accountability, and create spaces where everyone feels safe. Sometimes it’s a big protest. Other times, it’s a quiet conversation that opens someone’s eyes, or a small policy shift that makes a world of difference over time.
The real challenge? Staying engaged, even when the news is discouraging. It’s so tempting to just tune everything out and believe things will never get better. But if you look at history, progress is possible—even if it’s slow. The key is to keep asking questions, keep listening, and keep pushing for a world where everyone is treated with respect.
